ApiBaseUrl.Name: API Base URL
ApiBaseUrl.Hint: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API. The guided AI Provider Setup supplies presets for DeepSeek, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, and LM Studio.

ApiKey.Name: API Key
ApiKey.Hint: API key for the current API Base URL. It stays in this browser and is never synced to the world or other users. Manage it through AI Provider Setup, which masks the value and authorizes it only for the displayed endpoint. Leave blank for a keyless local server such as Ollama or LM Studio.

JevApiKey.Name: Jev API Key
JevApiKey.Hint: OpenRouter or TypeSafe AI key used only for Jev fast picks. Stored in this browser; manage it through AI Provider Setup.

JevTypeSafeEndpoint.Name: Jev TypeSafe Endpoint
JevTypeSafeEndpoint.Hint: Where a TypeSafe AI Jev key is sent: blank for api.typesafe.ai, or the address of your own CORS proxy. Manage it through AI Provider Setup.

JevSource.Name: Jev Source
JevSource.Hint: Where the separate Jev key is sent: OpenRouter or TypeSafe AI. Manage it through AI Provider Setup.

Model.Name: Model
Model.Hint: Model identifier, e.g. deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, gpt-6-luna, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash on OpenRouter, or any model your provider offers.

Temperature.Name: Creativity (temperature)
Temperature.Hint: Higher values give more creative (and less predictable) concepts. Grounding and selection operations always use temperature 0 for reliable local-model output.

MaxTokens.Name: Max response tokens
MaxTokens.Hint: Global upper limit for AI responses. Each operation applies a smaller production-safe cap where possible; reasoning is disabled so the allowance is reserved for complete structured output.

RequestTimeout.Name: Request timeout (seconds)
RequestTimeout.Hint: Abort a generation if the AI provider sends no data for this long. Responses are streamed, so slow models keep working as long as data keeps arriving. This only catches genuinely stalled connections.

RunTokenBudget.Name: Run token budget
RunTokenBudget.Hint: A run stops once it spends this many tokens across all its AI calls (default 60000). Raise it or set 0 to disable; reached limit stops the run instead of retrying forever.

RunDeadline.Name: Run deadline (minutes)
RunDeadline.Hint: Minutes before a run times out (default 5). Set 0 to turn the limit off.

FreeArchetype.Name: Free Archetype variant rule
FreeArchetype.Hint: When enabled, one-click characters gain the variant's extra archetype feat slot at each even level. Picks are validated staged: candidate-time prerequisite filtering plus slot-placement checks, and unprovable placements are left unresolved instead of guessed.

WhatsNew.Title: What's new in SimplySF2e
WhatsNew.MenuHint: See the latest changes to SimplySF2e. It also opens once by itself after an update that changes something you can see.
WhatsNew.Intro: SimplySF2e {version}: here is what changed since you last looked.
WhatsNew.BrokeBody: Use Copy bug report in the Generator's error box and send it, with a line on what you were doing, to whoever gave you the module.

ReviewFixes.Title: Fixes and a tidier setup
ReviewFixes.B1: Ysoki and G'folian characters now get their own ancestry feats.
ReviewFixes.B2: Creature spellcasters keep their cantrips at cantrip rank.
ReviewFixes.B3: Re-leveling a creature far down no longer gives zero or negative AC, saves or damage.
ReviewFixes.B4: Reskinning a world creature makes a fresh copy: full health, no conditions, GM-only ownership.
ReviewFixes.B5: An API Base URL that contains a password or key is refused, because players read it.

HuntFixes.Title: Fixes from a full code review
HuntFixes.B1: Encounter mode: Generate creates the actors in one go.
HuntFixes.B2: Generate with an empty prompt no longer creates the previous preview.
HuntFixes.B3: Shop and Treasure price ammunition per round, without a stray extra credit.
HuntFixes.B4: Re-level now handles very low levels and Trample correctly.
HuntFixes.B5: AI Provider Setup refuses to switch connection during a run, and Delete asks once.

ProgressTelemetry.Title: Step times and a simpler Welcome
ProgressTelemetry.B1: Progress card: each finished step shows how long it took.
ProgressTelemetry.B2: Progress card: the current step says "running".
ProgressTelemetry.B3: Welcome no longer numbers its sections.
ProgressTelemetry.B4: Welcome: the connection check lists its steps one per line.

ThemeSystem.Title: One look in every window
ThemeSystem.B1: Glow marks what is live: the main action, the active mode and a running progress card.
ThemeSystem.B2: Only labels, column headings and tags are in capitals; titles and buttons are not.
ThemeSystem.B3: Trait tags are square, and empty panels share one look.

SetupWiring.Title: Clearer setup windows
SetupWiring.B1: Welcome: the missing compendium warning has a Configure compendium sources button.
SetupWiring.B2: AI Provider Setup explains Save & test and Save & authorize.
SetupWiring.B3: AI Provider Setup shows when an API key or a Jev key is saved.
SetupWiring.B4: AI Provider Setup marks a rejected price field.
SetupWiring.B5: Item Forge: the prompt hint follows the item kind.

CopySweep.Title: Clearer wording
CopySweep.B1: Window titles, buttons and empty-state hints use the same names.
CopySweep.B2: Empty Shop, Treasure and Item Forge windows name the button to press next.
CopySweep.B3: Mode tooltips say what each mode builds.
CopySweep.B4: Provider notes read "Not yet tested", and a failed Welcome connect reads "Connection failed".

ShellConsistency.Title: Tidier windows
ShellConsistency.B1: Discard, Delete and Reset are red and sit apart from the main action.
ShellConsistency.B2: Numbers line up in tables and the token report.
ShellConsistency.B3: Empty panels are more compact than before.
ShellConsistency.B4: Long model and connection names wrap instead of being cut off.
ShellConsistency.B5: Encounter members, review lists and the Forge, Shop and Treasure readiness row match the Generator's layout.

RunGuards.Title: Fewer ways to lose work
RunGuards.B1: Create all actors is disabled when every encounter member is set to 0.
RunGuards.B2: A merchant or hoard that cannot be verified or removed is named; its draft is discarded.
RunGuards.B3: AI Provider Setup asks before switching, creating or deleting a connection with unsaved edits.
RunGuards.B4: AI Provider Setup keeps your edits when loading models.
RunGuards.B5: AI Provider Setup refuses to switch connections while a run is in progress.

OneScreenWelcome.Title: Set up in one screen
OneScreenWelcome.B1: Welcome connects your AI in one step: pick a provider, paste a key, press Connect.
OneScreenWelcome.B2: Connect loads the model list, tests the model and offers a sample monster.
OneScreenWelcome.B3: A failed connect leaves your previous setup untouched.

RelevelAbilities.Title: Re-leveled creatures keep their numbers in step
RelevelAbilities.B1: Re-level rebuilds the area blasts, auras and filled glossary abilities the module made.
RelevelAbilities.B2: Re-level: published abilities keep their text.

Aura.Title: Auras with real numbers
Aura.B1: Creatures can have auras that call for a save and apply a condition.
Aura.B2: Auras can also deal damage each turn.
Aura.B3: Radius, save DC, condition value and damage come from GM Core and the creature's level.
Aura.B4: The aura shows on the canvas; you apply the result.

AreaBlast.Title: Breaths and blasts with real numbers
AreaBlast.B1: Creature breath weapons and blasts can now be working abilities.
AreaBlast.B2: Area, damage and DC come from GM Core for the creature's level.
AreaBlast.B3: A limited blast can be recharged.

BlankAbilities.Title: Creature abilities get real values again
BlankAbilities.B1: Constrict, Greater Constrict, Swallow Whole, Engulf, Trample, Frightful Presence and Stench now get filled values.
BlankAbilities.B2: Values come from GM Core tables and published creatures, scaled to the creature's level.
BlankAbilities.B3: Trample uses the creature's own strike.
BlankAbilities.B4: An ability that cannot be filled is left out and named in the console.

ClearerErrors.Title: Clearer error messages and bug reports
ClearerErrors.B1: Error messages say what went wrong and what to do next.
ClearerErrors.B2: After you copy a bug report, an Open GitHub issue button opens the issue form.
ClearerErrors.B3: The report is never put in the link.

RunDeadline.Title: Runs stop after 5 minutes
RunDeadline.B1: Runs stop after 5 minutes by default, so a stuck request cannot hang the Generator.
RunDeadline.B2: Change the limit in Module Settings: SimplySF2e, Run deadline (minutes).
RunDeadline.B3: Set it to 0 to turn the limit off.

RunCost.Title: Run cost
RunCost.B1: The token report shows run cost when your provider reports it, as OpenRouter does.
RunCost.B2: For other providers, enter optional per-1M-token prices in AI Provider Setup.
RunCost.B3: Estimates from those prices are marked with ≈.

RunBudget.Title: Per-run token budget
RunBudget.B1: A run stops at a token budget instead of retrying forever.
RunBudget.B3: The limit is a world setting.

ProviderRetry.Title: More resilient provider requests
ProviderRetry.B1: On a rate limit or transient server error, SimplySF2e waits and retries once.
ProviderRetry.B2: It honors the provider's Retry-After value when given.
ProviderRetry.B3: Ambiguous server errors that may already have been billed are not retried.
ProviderRetry.B4: Cancelling a run also stops the retry.

Multiclass.Title: Multiclass, Tech Core ancestries and more
Multiclass.B1: With Free Archetype on, choose a second class in Multiclass, or let the AI choose.
Multiclass.B2: The dedication goes in the first archetype slot, and later slots favor its feats.
Multiclass.B3: Mystic, Witchwarper and Technomancer dedications get their own spell list.
Multiclass.B4: Living Hologram and SRO characters get their size chosen for you.
Multiclass.B5: Item Forge installs projectile-weapon upgrades and says which requested upgrades did not fit.

ClassFixes.Title: Every class builds cleanly
ClassFixes.B1: Player characters of every class now build from level 1 to 20.
ClassFixes.B2: Feat choices check planned attributes and skill ranks at each level.
ClassFixes.B3: General feat slots can also hold skill feats, as in the system.
ClassFixes.B4: Operative specializations keep the feat they need.
ClassFixes.B5: If no legal feat exists for a slot, it stays empty and a whisper lists it.

TechCore.Title: Mechanic and Technomancer player characters
TechCore.B1: SimplySF2e now needs the Starfinder 2e system 1.6 or later.
TechCore.B2: Player characters can be Mechanics or Technomancers from Tech Core.
TechCore.B3: A Technomancer gets the magic hack that matches its programming language.
TechCore.B4: A Mechanic with the Drone exocortex gets a reminder to set up the drone by hand.

UiRefresh.Title: Easier to read, more Starfinder
UiRefresh.B1: Small labels and table headings are larger.
UiRefresh.B2: Input fields have clearer borders than before.
UiRefresh.B3: After a preview appears, Create is the main button and Generate offers another version.
UiRefresh.B4: Icons now fit Starfinder: a microchip for the Generator, gears for the Item Forge.
UiRefresh.B5: Item Forge wording now fits Starfinder.

CreatureArt.Title: Creature art keeps its token
CreatureArt.B1: With an art module, a generated creature keeps the similar bestiary creature's token art and scale.
CreatureArt.B2: The token no longer reuses the bestiary portrait.
CreatureArt.B3: The token is named after the new creature.
CreatureArt.B4: Encounter copies are numbered in their token name too.

WhatsNew.Title: What's new
WhatsNew.B1: This window opens once after an update that changes something you can see.
WhatsNew.B2: Reopen it any time with /sf2e whatsnew.

ReskinTrample.Title: Reskin keeps Trample in step
ReskinTrample.B1: Reskin: a Trample the module built names the renamed melee Strike.
ReskinTrample.B2: Trample on published creatures is not changed.

OneCredstick.Title: One Credstick per hoard
OneCredstick.B1: A hoard's leftover credits go on one Credstick, up to 5,000,000 credits.
OneCredstick.B2: This replaces the old split into several 100,000-credit sticks.
OneCredstick.B3: NPC and player-character Credstick coin now reaches the full treasure budget at every level.
OneCredstick.B4: It used to stop at 100,000 credits, which cut level 13+ budgets short.

UiPolish.Title: Cleaner windows
UiPolish.B1: Previews fold the token report into one line.
UiPolish.B2: Encounter cards show stats as a grid.
UiPolish.B3: The character review lists what to check.
UiPolish.B4: AI Provider Setup and Compendium Sources are easier to scan, with a pack filter.
UiPolish.B5: Narrow windows are easier to read.

FasterEncounters.Title: Faster encounters
FasterEncounters.B1: Encounter mode builds several creatures at the same time.
FasterEncounters.B2: Large encounters are ready sooner than before.

Treasure.Title: Treasure hoards
Treasure.B1: A new Treasure window opens from the Actors sidebar button or /sf2e treasure.
Treasure.B2: It fills one encounter's or a whole level's treasure budget.
Treasure.B3: It uses real Starfinder items and credits.
Treasure.B4: The result is created as a loot actor.

Relevel.Title: Re-level a creature
Relevel.B1: In Reskin mode, set a new level for the copy.
Relevel.B2: AC, HP, attacks, saves, skills and DCs move to GM Core values for that level.
Relevel.B3: Each stat keeps its relative strength.

Sources.MenuHint: Choose which compendium packs SimplySF2e draws abilities, spells, feats, and equipment from.
Sources.Title: Compendium Sources
Sources.Hint: SimplySF2e scanned this world's Item compendiums. Choose the packs each category may draw from; homebrew and module packs work too. Leaving a category empty uses the SF2e system pack defaults.
Sources.NonePacksFound: No compendium packs with matching content were found in this world. Install an SF2e or homebrew compendium pack, then reopen this window.
Sources.ResetConfirm: Reset every category to the SF2e system pack defaults? Unsaved changes in this window are lost.
Sources.ResetDone: Compendium sources reset to the SF2e system pack defaults.
Sources.FilterPlaceholder: Filter by pack or module name
Sources.NoMatches: No pack matches this filter. Ticked packs stay ticked; clear the filter to see every pack.

Preview.MulticlassNotPlaced: Multiclass: {class}. Its dedication was not placed; review the archetype slots in Foundry.
Preview.PCSignaturePlan: Planned signature choices: {selected}/{total}. Choices are rechecked against real spells during creation; missing or rejected choices stay regular and need manual review.
Preview.PCBaseSpellPlan: Base spell plan only: prepared classes prepare each listed pick; spontaneous classes learn it at the listed rank. Review empty slots, signature spells, and restricted subclass or feat bonuses (such as curriculum or divine font) in Foundry.
Preview.PCVariableSpellPlan: Base spell plan only. Verify the tradition against your bloodline or patron; if none was selected, configure spellcasting in Foundry. Review empty slots, signature spells, subclass-granted spells, and feat bonuses after creation.
Preview.PCApproximateSpellPlan: This class has no verified casting profile yet. Spellcasting uses a generic spontaneous approximation; review casting mode, tradition, slots, and spells in Foundry before play.
Preview.FromCompendium: Pulled from a bestiary ability glossary pack
Preview.NotFound: No compendium match found. This entry will be skipped

ItemForge.Title: SimplySF2e Item Forge
ItemForge.SourcesDetail: Draws from the packs chosen in Compendium Sources.
ItemForge.PromptPlaceholder: e.g. A scorched visor that shields the wearer's mind and lets them see in the dark...

Placeholder.Wondrous: Describe the item's effect, how it looks, and who carries or wears it.
Placeholder.Weapon: Describe the weapon's form, its wear, and any feature that sets it apart, such as a scorch mark or a cracked grip.
Placeholder.Armor: Describe the armor's material, its wear, and any module fitted to it, such as a salvaged shield module.
Placeholder.Augmentation: Describe the implant: the body part it replaces or extends, and what it does for the wearer, such as a built-in scanner.
Placeholder.Crystal: Describe the crystal: its color, how it behaves, and what it powers or does, such as humming near hot metal.

ItemForge.NoEffects: No usable passive effects survived validation, so the item will be created as flavor-only. Press Generate another version for a mechanical one.
ItemForge.Created: Created item "{name}". Drag it from the Items directory onto a character sheet.
ItemForge.CreateFailed: Foundry did not return a created item. The preview is still available to retry.
ItemForge.CreatedPresentationFailed: The item was created, but its sheet could not be displayed. Open it from the Items directory; do not create it again.
ItemForge.KindsUnavailable: No supported published passive effects match this level and rarity for: {kinds}. These effect kinds are not offered. Raise the item level or rarity to offer them.
ItemForge.UpgradesSkipped: Not installed: {upgrades}. Either this base has no free upgrade slot, or the upgrade is not made for this base's weapon group.
ItemForge.MacroFailed: The item was saved, but its activation macro could not be completed. Its passive effects remain; check the console before using the activated power.
ItemForge.KindWeaponHint: A real weapon with level-appropriate equipment grade and upgrades
ItemForge.KindArmorHint: Real armor with level-appropriate equipment grade and upgrades
ItemForge.KindAugmentationHint: Implanted tech, biotech, magitech, or necrograft
ItemForge.KindCrystalHint: Magic crystal for a solarian; general passive effects, not solar weapon damage
ItemForge.NoBaseItems: No {kind} items were found in this world's compendiums. Is the SF2e equipment pack installed?
ItemForge.EmptyHint: Describe an item and press Generate. The preview appears here before anything is created.

Loot.CustomItem: Generated by SimplySF2e. No compendium match was found for this item, so it stands in as treasure with an estimated value. Replace it with the real item if you have it.

Equipment.CustomItem: Generated by SimplySF2e. No compendium match was found for this item, so it stands in as plain gear at an estimated price. Replace it with the real item if you have it.

BugReport.Tooltip: Copies the error, the failed step, your form, settings and versions so you can paste them to the module author. API keys are never included.
BugReport.Copied: Bug report copied. Paste it to the module author.
BugReport.ManualHint: This browser blocked the clipboard. The report is selected below: press Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on a Mac) to copy it.
BugReport.Failed: Could not build the bug report. The browser console (F12) has the details.

Errors.GMOnly: Only a GM can use SimplySF2e generation and provider setup. Ask a GM to do this.
Errors.NoPrompt: Fill in the Describe box first, then try again.
Errors.NoBaseUrl: No API Base URL is set. Open AI Provider Setup and enter your provider's address. It is also under Welcome > Advanced.
Errors.NoModel: No model is set. Enter a model name in AI Provider Setup (also under Welcome > Advanced) or Module Settings → SimplySF2e, then try again.
Errors.InsecureKeyEndpoint: This AI address starts with http://, so your API key would travel unencrypted. The key was not sent. Use an https:// address, or a provider on this computer or your local network.
Errors.MixedContentProvider: Foundry is open over https://, but the AI provider address starts with http://, and the browser blocks that. Use an https:// API Base URL in AI Provider Setup, or open Foundry over http:// if both are on your local network. AI Provider Setup is also under Welcome > Advanced.
Errors.ApiError: The AI provider returned an error ({status}): {detail} {hint}
Errors.ProviderError: The AI provider reported an error: {detail} Check the provider's dashboard for billing, credit or key problems, then try again.
Errors.ApiAuthHint: Check the API key, then use AI Provider Setup to authorize it for this exact endpoint.
Errors.ApiNotFoundHint: Check the API Base URL and the model name. The server may not offer the chat API at that address.
Errors.ApiRateLimitHint: Wait and retry, or check the provider account's quota and billing status.
Errors.ApiServerHint: The provider is unavailable or had an internal error. Wait a few minutes and try again, or check its status page.
Errors.ApiRequestHint: Check the API Base URL and the model name, then try again.
Errors.NetworkError: Could not reach the AI provider: {message}. Check the API Base URL and your internet connection. For a local or self-hosted provider, make sure it is running and allows requests from Foundry (CORS).
Errors.InvalidResponse: The AI provider sent back a reply the module could not read. Check that the API Base URL points to the provider's chat API, which usually ends in /v1.
Errors.EmptyResponse: The AI provider sent back an empty answer. Check the provider's status page and the model name, then try again.
Errors.ReasoningWithoutJson: The AI sent back reasoning text but no answer. Try again. If it keeps happening, choose a different model.
Errors.Truncated: The AI ran out of room before finishing its answer. Try again, use a shorter prompt, or choose a different model. Raise Max response tokens in Module Settings only if its value is below {max}.
Errors.RunBudgetExceeded: This run used its {limit}-token budget and stopped. To allow more, raise Run token budget in Module Settings → SimplySF2e (0 turns the limit off), then start a new run.
Errors.RunDeadline: This run passed its time limit and stopped. To allow more time, raise Run deadline (minutes) in Module Settings → SimplySF2e (0 turns the limit off), then start a new run.
Errors.Timeout: The AI provider sent no data for {seconds} seconds, so the request was stopped. Check the API Base URL and the provider's status. If the provider is slow, raise Request timeout (seconds) in Module Settings → SimplySF2e, then try again.
Errors.BadJson: The AI answer was in a format the module could not read. Try again. If it keeps failing, choose a different model.
Errors.BadStructure: The AI answer was incomplete ({detail}). Try again, or choose a more capable model.
Errors.NoBestiaryScaffold: No usable NPC actor was found in the enabled Bestiary Actors sources. Open Compendium Sources, enable a pack with NPC actors, then try again.
Errors.WrongSystem: SimplySF2e only works in a Starfinder 2e world. Open a world that uses the Starfinder Second Edition (sf2e) game system.

Shop.Prompt: What does it sell, and who runs it?
Shop.PromptPlaceholder: A cramped weapons stall on Absalom Station run by a retired soldier who only sells what she has field-tested.
Shop.SourcesDetail: Stock comes only from your equipment compendiums, at their published prices.
Shop.LevelHint: Stock is this level or lower.
Shop.NoEquipmentPack: No equipment compendium is enabled. Check Compendium Sources.
Shop.NoCandidates: No equipment at this level and rarity was found in your compendiums. Raise Rarest stock or Shop level, or enable more packs in Compendium Sources.
Shop.NoStock: The AI picked nothing from the offered items. Press Generate again.
Shop.EmptyHint: Describe the shop, then press Generate shop to stock it from your sf2e equipment compendium.
Shop.StockTotal: Total stock value: {total} credits. Prices are the compendium's own.
Shop.AllRemoved: Every item was removed. Press Generate another shop to restock.
Shop.Dropped: Picks left out because they were not on the offered list: {count}.
Shop.RollbackSurvivor: Merchant "{name}" still exists. The draft was discarded to prevent a duplicate; remove it manually before trying again.

Relevel.Label: New level
Relevel.Hint: Change it to re-level the copy. Each number keeps its Starfinder GM Core scale (high, moderate and so on) at the new level.
Relevel.UnchangedSummary: What else moves, and what stays
Relevel.Unchanged: Area blasts, auras and filled glossary abilities the module built are rebuilt for the new level. Published abilities keep their text. Spells and their ranks, the ritual DC, gear, and Elite/Weak stay as they are. Attributes and skills also move, and very low ones (below every GM Core scale) stay put.
Relevel.Notice: The copy is moved to level {level} with the GM Core tables. Rules, traits, spells, and items are copied unchanged. The original creature is not modified.

Treasure.PartyHint: Party size only shows an "each" figure. The budget is per party, so it does not change.

Treasure.NoItems: Nothing fit the budget. Press Generate again.
Treasure.EmptyHint: Set the party level and amount, then press Generate hoard to fill it from your sf2e equipment compendium.
